headline: Wichita State details Paul Mills extension worth up to $2.3M a year by 2030-31
summary: Wichita State released terms of men's basketball coach Paul Mills' contract extension running July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031. Mills can make up to $1.789 million in year one — including $1.4 million guaranteed, roughly $314,000 for off-court contributions and a $75,000 retention bonus — with total pay climbing past $1.9 million in year two and topping out at just over $2.3 million in the final year, a sign of how far mid-major coaching money has moved in the revenue-share era.

headline: Judge Sweeney clarifies fifth-year injunction: roster caps and rev-share caps still stand
summary: Colorado U.S. District Judge Charlotte Sweeney issued a clarifying order stating that her class-wide injunction granting high school Class of 2022 athletes a fifth season does not override NCAA transfer rules, House-settlement roster caps or revenue-sharing caps. Athletes who skipped the transfer portal window cannot now transfer, players who signed pro contracts are excluded, and returners can only reclaim spots that are already open — limiting the roster and budget chaos programs feared heading into 2026-27.

headline: Federal judge certifies nationwide class, grants Class of 2022 athletes a fifth season
summary: U.S. District Judge Charlotte Sweeney certified a nationwide class in Wisne v. NCAA — the basketball-led antitrust case fronted by Northern Colorado's Brock Wisne and Minnesota's Cade Tyson — and issued a preliminary injunction ordering the NCAA to declare immediately eligible athletes who began college play in 2022-23 and exhausted eligibility this spring under the old four-in-five rule. The ruling, which followed an earlier Ohio state-court injunction won by two dozen men's and women's basketball players in July, blows open rosters and NIL/rev-share budgets for 2026-27 and drew the SEC and Big Ten deeper into the push for federal eligibility protection.

headline: Eleven athletes, led by basketball players, file class action over NCAA's new eligibility model
summary: A group of 11 Division I athletes headlined by Minnesota basketball player Cade Tyson and Northern Colorado basketball player Brock Wisne filed a federal antitrust class action in the District of Colorado, alleging the NCAA's new five-year eligibility rule — implemented June 24 — unlawfully denies thousands of athletes an additional season and the NIL and revenue-share money that comes with it. The suit seeks to cover athletes across men's and women's basketball, baseball and track who were excluded from the rule's grandfathering.

headline: Basketball players sue NCAA within 24 hours of new age-based five-year eligibility rule
summary: Less than a day after the NCAA Division I Cabinet approved a five-seasons-in-five-years eligibility model — which starts the clock at enrollment or the academic year after an athlete's 19th birthday and all but eliminates medical redshirt waivers — a group of 15 college basketball players filed suit in Ohio state court in Cincinnati. The players, all from the high school Class of 2022, argue the rule arbitrarily denies them a fifth season and the NIL and revenue-share earnings attached to it; the case produced a preliminary injunction from Judge Christopher Wagner the following month.

headline: NCAA permanently bans four Alabama State players for fixing a game for $2,000
summary: The NCAA Division I Committee on Infractions ruled that four former Alabama State men's basketball players — Amarr Knox, Shawn Fulcher, Corey Hines and Tony Madlock — committed Level I sports betting violations by manipulating the outcome of a December 2024 game at Southern Miss in exchange for a combined $2,000 in bribes, and declared them permanently ineligible. The negotiated resolution is part of the widening game-fixing scandal that has drawn federal charges and NCAA integrity probes across more than a dozen Division I programs.
